Google Maps Said a Hike Would Take 5 Hours. B.C. Rescuers Pointed Out How Wrong That Was

2026-07-20 CTV News Google Maps, hiking, trail navigation, British Columbia, search and rescue, navigation safety, outdoor recreation, ETA accuracy
Read the source article

Quick summary

Hikers recently rescued from an extremely challenging trail in British Columbia had planned their trip using Google Maps, which estimated a 5-hour hike — prompting rescue teams to warn about the perils of relying on consumer navigation apps for backcountry travel.

Key takeaways

  • Hikers used Google Maps to plan a trip on an extremely challenging B.C. trail, with an estimated 5-hour duration
  • Rescuers pointed out that the estimate was dangerously inaccurate for the terrain involved
  • The incident prompted a warning about the dangers of relying on Google Maps for backcountry hiking
  • Search and rescue teams emphasise that consumer navigation apps are not designed for wilderness trail assessment
  • The case highlights the gap between urban navigation ETA algorithms and real-world backcountry conditions
